sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Bottom-Up Approach**: Reverses traditional top-down planning by ensuring plans originate at the **Gram Sabha** and ascend to district and state levels.
• **Democratic Decentralization**: Implemented constitutionally via **Part IX** and **Part IX-A** of the Constitution, empowering local bodies.
• **District Planning Committee (DPC)**: Mandated under **Article 243ZD** to consolidate plans prepared by panchayats and municipalities in the district.
• **Metropolitan Planning Committee (MPC)**: Mandated under **Article 243ZE** to prepare development plans for metropolitan areas.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Devolution of the **3Fs**—Funds, Functions, and Functionaries—to local self-governments.

items.definition: A comprehensive holistic plan prepared by every Gram Panchayat annually, converging resources for economic development and social justice.
Constitutional body under Article 243ZD responsible for consolidating rural and urban local plans into a draft district development plan.
Constitutional body under Article 243I/243Y that reviews the financial position of panchayats and municipalities and recommends tax/duty sharing.
73rd & 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts (1992); Gadgil Formula; Sarkaria Commission; Punchhi Commission; 2nd ARC Reports.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Kerala Model**: Pioneer in decentralized planning via 'People's Plan Campaign' (1996), devolving substantial plan funds directly to local bodies.
• **Backward Districts**: NITI Aayog's **Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP)** and **Aspirational Blocks Programme (ABP)** focus decentralized monitoring on lagging regions.
• **Driving Advantages**: Overcomes uniform national policy failures by addressing localized agro-climatic, tribal, and regional specificities.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Severe lack of administrative capacity at local levels, elite capture of Gram Sabhas, inadequate own-source revenue (OSR) generation, and delayed constitution of DPCs.
• **Policy Interventions**: E-governance portals like **e-GramSwaraj**, capacity building via **RGSA (Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan)**, and outcome-based performance grants.

items.title: Mnemonic for Local Government Articles
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'PMP-FI' (Panchayats, Municipalities, Planning, Finance, Inter-se)
• **Decoded Meaning**: Part IX (Panchayats 243-243O), Part IX-A (Municipalities 243P-243ZG), DPC (243ZD), MPC (243ZE), Finance Commissions (243I & 243Y).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly matches constitutional articles to their exact local governance domains.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Remember the 3Fs for effective devolution: Funds without Functions fail; Functions without Functionaries stall; all three together ensure true Decentralization.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that District Planning Committees (DPCs) are optional or formed by the Central Government. In reality, DPCs are **mandated by Article 243ZD** of the Constitution and are constituted at the **District level by State Governments**, not the Centre.

Mains Value Addition: Quote the 2nd Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC) recommendation that decentralized planning requires 'Activity Mapping'—clearly segregating functions between state governments and various tiers of panchayats to eliminate role duplication.

keyTakeaways: Decentralized planning shifts economic decision-making from central authorities to grassroots institutions like Gram Sabhas and DPCs.
Constitutional backing through Articles 243ZD and 243ZE mandates district and metropolitan planning committees to aggregate local plans.
Effective decentralization depends entirely on the robust devolution of Funds, Functions, and Functionaries (the 3Fs) to local self-governments.
